findings.title: Ensure moves the source to whichever account was noted last, so deleting that account orphans the source.
findings.body:
The identity key is (organization, provider, external_account_id), but more than one connector account can share an external ID, for example after a reconnect while the old connector still exists. Each `NoteConnectorAccount` call overwrites `connector_account_id` with the account being noted.

How it breaks: connector A is created first, then connector B for the same AWS account, so the source points at B. Later, A's org selection is updated (source_service hunk 2), which notes A and moves the source back to A. When A is deleted, the FK sets `connector_account_id` to NULL. `LoadNextDueForUpdateSkipLocked` then skips the source, so nothing is synced even though B is still connected. Syncing only starts again if B happens to be noted later.

Fix: when the linked account is deleted, re-link the source to another live connector account with the same organization, provider and external ID instead of just clearing the link. Alternatively, only re-point a source that is unlinked or whose current account is gone.

findings.title: cloudfront is imported directly but listed as `// indirect`.
findings.body: `pkg/itam/cloudfront.go` imports `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/cloudfront` directly, but go.mod marks the module `// indirect` and lists it in the indirect block. Running `go mod tidy` would rewrite go.mod, so any CI check that runs tidy and diffs the result will fail. Move the line into the direct `require` block without the comment.

held.title: Backfill links and schedules every AWS connector account, including disabled ones.
held.body:
At runtime a source is only created or made due when an AWS account is created, enabled or reconnected (`NoteConnectorAccount`). The backfill ignores whether the account is enabled: every AWS `connector_accounts` row gets a source that is linked and due now (`next_sync_at = NOW()`). Disabled or revoked accounts will therefore be claimed by the worker on its first run, which opens connector sessions for accounts the user turned off.

The tie-break has the same gap. It uses only `updated_at DESC`, so when an external id has both a recently disabled account and an older enabled one, the disabled one wins the link.

I could not see whether the worker checks the account status before syncing; if it does, only the wrong link remains. Fix: filter or order on the account's enabled/active state, the same condition the service uses before calling `NoteConnectorAccount`. For example, add the status to the WHERE clause, or sort enabled rows first before `updated_at DESC`.
